lines.text: On a mountain in New Mexico, astronomers aim a laser at the Moon.
The pulse of light leaves the Earth… and crosses three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres of empty space.
There, it finds a small mirror, left on the Moon by the Apollo astronauts in 1969.
Two and a half seconds later, a handful of photons come home… and that tiny delay tells us exactly how far away the Moon is.
